I am 68 years old, farming here in Quzhou for 51 years. My land is 30.4 mu, and I run the wheat-maize double cropping like most households on the North China Plain. I also keep a small piece for millet because my family likes to eat it and it sells decently at the town market. With 8 people in the household and some working outside, I have enough hands for the busy seasons but I still hire the combine harvester — nobody cuts by hand anymore on this scale.

Let me think through this year crop by crop.

**Winter wheat** — I plant around middle of October after the maize comes off. I use Jimai 22 or a similar improved variety, the seed dealer in town has good stock. For 30 mu class farm like mine, I know the soil here is alkaline calcareous loam, moderate fertility because we've been double-cropping for decades. Last year I put about 18 kg urea-N before sowing as base with DAP, then topdressed about 8 kg N at jointing in March. That gave me around 500 kg/mu. I'll do similar this year — maybe 25-26 kg N total, 8 kg P2O5, 6 kg K2O. Wheat here needs 3 irrigations: one after sowing to settle the seed, one at jointing (most important), one at grain filling if the spring is dry. Pesticide — I spray once for aphids and wheat midge around heading, and once herbicide in late winter for bindweed and shepherd's purse. So 2 applications usually, sometimes 3 if stripe rust shows up.

**Summer maize** — Straight after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed with the no-till planter, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335 hybrid. No tillage saves time because the window is tight — we have maybe 5 days between wheat combine and maize sowing. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing (around 15 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu base), then topdress urea around 10-12 kg N at the big flare stage (V10-V12). Total N about 25-27 kg/mu. Maize needs 2 irrigations usually — one at sowing if soil is dry, one at tasseling which is critical. Pesticide: one spray for corn borer and armyworm at whorl stage, sometimes a second for aphids. Expect around 550-600 kg/mu, I got 580 last year.

**Millet** — Small plot, maybe 2 mu, spring-planted in April. Millet is tough, doesn't need much. I use an improved variety from the agri station, Zhangzagu series. Light fertilizer — 8 kg N, 4 kg P, 3 kg K. Maybe one irrigation if spring is really dry, often zero because millet handles drought. One pesticide spray for aphids. I plough this plot because it's separate from the main wheat-maize rotation. Yield around 300 kg/mu for millet is good.

My thinking: I keep fertilizer slightly generous — an extra bag of urea costs maybe 130 yuan, but losing 50 kg of wheat is 60+ yuan gone and my family's food. At 68 I know my fields well, I don't need to experiment. Stick with what works.
